symbols.name: dollar_path
symbols.doc: Parse a ``$.a.b`` / ``$.l[0]`` field string into expr.py path steps.

symbols.name: resolve
symbols.doc: ``data #> path`` with the two nulls kept apart (§7.4(1b)).

symbols.name: text_of
symbols.doc: ``->>`` for the values the frame actually orders on: text or null.

symbols.name: numeric_value
symbols.doc: §7.2 item 5's numeric read, Python half, over the exact parse (B7).

symbols.name: parse_computed
symbols.doc: Parse each computed column's expression once. [(name, ast), …] in entry order. The gate has already accepted these (§4.5: the server gates before either pane runs); a parse error here propagates loudly.

symbols.name: computed_values
symbols.doc: Operation 2 on one row: evaluate each AST on ``record_f``.

symbols.name: keep_by_filter
symbols.doc: Operation 3 on one row: expr truthiness of the filter, on record_f.

symbols.name: field_reader
symbols.doc: One reader for op 6's and op 8's chosen field (§4.4 row 6's two forms).

symbols.name: _frame_order_key
symbols.doc: ``ORDER BY (data ->> 'ts'), key`` within one partition — text order, which for the seed's fixed-width UTC ISO-8601 is time order, with SQL NULL last (Postgres's ASC default) and ``key`` the tiebreak (§7.4).

symbols.name: rolling_averages
symbols.doc: Operation 8: ``avg(<numeric read>) OVER (w ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`` — {row index: value}.

symbols.name: _compared_value
symbols.doc: §7.1's comparison rule: the record minus its ordering key — the spec's own spelling, over the EXACT parse (B7 rules op 9's comparison onto ``record_d``: jsonb compares numbers as numerics, exactly, and so does a dict of int/Decimal). Content equality, key order irrelevant — never serialised text.

symbols.name: changed_flags
symbols.doc: Operation 9: ``lag(data - 'ts') OVER w IS DISTINCT FROM (data - 'ts')`` — {row index: kept?}.

symbols.name: aggregate
symbols.doc: Operation 6 over one group of rows (the whole pick for SCALAR, one bucket for BUCKET).

symbols.name: bucket_label
symbols.doc: Operation 7's bucket for one row, as the label BOTH panes key by.

symbols.name: row_sort_key
symbols.doc: §7.4's total order for one row, routed through W9's ``sort_key``.
